g202.text: The Sun! Every evening, it goes. Every morning, it comes back. Why?

g203.text: One, the Sun moves away. Two, the Earth turns. Three, clouds hide the Sun.

g301a.text: A little owl is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

g301m.text: It hides somewhere new each time, so keep your eyes open!

g301b.text: You against the Buddies! Lock in first with your fingers. One finger for every point.

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

g501.text: Round one! Why does the Sun come back? Show me your fingers!

g503.text: One! I see the Sun move across the sky!

g504.text: Three! It was cloudy last night, so the clouds hid the Sun.

g505.text: Two! The Earth turns, just like my spinning globe!

g601.text: Look closer. This is the sky from our window, speeded up.

g602p.text: First, the Sun comes up behind the blocks, and the sky gets bright. That is day time!

g603b.text: Then the sky goes dark, and the lamps come on. That is nighttime: pyjama time!

g605.text: Look, there are no clouds tonight, and still no Sun. So clouds are not hiding the Sun!

g607b.text: Then it is morning again, and night again. Day, night, day, night: it changes, and it repeats!

g701m.text: But why does it keep repeating?

g702.text: A globe is our Earth. A torch is our Sun. The red dot is Singapore.

g703p.text: Watch. The torch stays still, and only the globe turns.

g704b.text: The red dot faces the torch, so it is day time.

g705m.text: Now it turns away, into the dark, so it is nighttime!

g706b.text: It keeps turning, so the red dot comes into the light again.

g707.text: The answer is two: the Earth turns! Two fingers? One finger up!

g709r.text: Rotation means the Earth spins round and round, like my globe when I flick it!

g801.text: Oh! So the Sun only looks as if it moves!

g901.text: Be the little red dot! Shrink down. Quietly.

g902.text: You are a tiny dot on the Earth: Singapore.

g903.text: Your side of the Earth faces the Sun, so it is day time!

g904.text: The Earth turns, and you turn away from the Sun. Now it is nighttime, and you can see the stars!

g905.text: The Earth keeps turning, and the light comes back. Good morning!

g1002.text: The repeated change between day and night is caused by the rotation of the Earth. This rotation takes 24 hours.

g1003p.text: So one full turn takes 24 hours: one day and one night!

g1104p.text: Let me check. Day changes into night, so it changes. It happens again and again, so it repeats!

g1105b.text: The same changes, again and again, like my school week. That is a repeated pattern!

g1101.text: Yes, Basil! A repeated pattern of change is called a cycle.

g1103.text: Cycles are repeated patterns of change. They happen in living and non-living things.

g1201.text: My pencil gets shorter and shorter, so it changes. That means it is a cycle!

g1202.text: Something is not right. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

g1205p.text: The pencil changes, but it never grows long again, so the change does not repeat.

g1301.text: Then look down there, at the traffic light! I think it is a cycle.

g1304b.text: It changes and it repeats, just like day and night, so it is a cycle too!

g1401.text: Show me your score hand! One finger or more? You beat the Buddies. Two fingers? High five!

g1402.text: Did you spot the owl? It was on the tree outside the window! Tell someone at home.

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

g1501.text: The Earth is non-living. Do living things have cycles too?

g1502.text: Good question, Momo! A hen, a chick and a teddy bear will show us.
